title: Standardization of Entity Identification and Reporting
summary: The concept of 'name' has evolved from a simple manual entry field in paper-based customs declarations (2014) to a structured, digitized requirement within the AEO and Cargo Declaration frameworks (2024-2025). The evolution reflects a shift toward mandatory data fields for specific stakeholders (carriers, agents, consignors) and formal procedures for reporting business identity changes.

evolution.scope: Expanded from simple importer identification to comprehensive stakeholder identification (carriers, agents, consignors, focal points).
evolution.procedure: Shifted from static entry to dynamic reporting requirements for business identity changes.
evolution.structure: Transitioned from unstructured text fields to mandatory, categorized data segments in digital systems.

timeline.change: Initial use of 'name' as a manual placeholder for importers in paper-based certification.
Formalization of 'name' as a mandatory data field in digital cargo declaration segments for carriers, agents, and consignors.
Introduction of formal procedures for reporting changes to business names and identity for AEO-certified entities.
Standardization of 'name' fields for focal point officers in customs station reporting.

Certificate of Utilization: This form serves as a formal certification confirming that imported goods have been used exclusively for the construction of pre-fabricated buildings in accordance with approved designs. It serves as an official declaration that no imported materials were misused during the construction process.
Bill of Entry: The certification process requires the specification of the bill of entry number and date corresponding to the goods cleared through the customs office or station.
Bonded Warehouse: The importer must provide their bond license number and the relevant issuance date as part of the verification details required in the certification document.
Trade Association: The certification requires validation through the signature, name, designation, and official seal of an authorized official from the relevant association or chamber, such as the BGMEA or BKMEA.

Conveyance Arrival and Departure: This standing order specifies the mandatory data fields for the general segment of a cargo declaration that must be submitted upon the arrival or departure of a conveyance. The required details include voyage information, shipping agent particulars, cargo totals, transport specifications, tonnage figures, and feeder operator details for both containerized and non-containerized cargo.
Shipping Agent: The cargo declaration process requires the mandatory submission of carrier and shipping agent identification details, including their official code, name, and address.
Container: The cargo declaration must include precise counts of containers and their corresponding gross weight as part of the total cargo assessment for transit or clearance.
Master of the Vessel: The vessel master's details must be formally declared in the transport section of the cargo declaration as part of the mandatory documentation required by customs authorities.
Vessel: Operational instructions require the reporting of specific vessel identification details, such as the name, nationality, registration number, and IMO number, within the cargo declaration's transport segment.

Manifest: This instruction mandates the specific data fields required to be completed within the waybill segment of a cargo declaration. The declaration must capture comprehensive details regarding the conveyance, consignor, consignee, transport modes, goods characteristics, and declared values to ensure proper customs processing.
Shipping Agent: The shipping agent must provide specific identification details, including code, name, and address, as part of the mandatory cargo declaration requirements.
Exporter: The declaration must include the code, name, and address of the exporter for all cargo entries.
Consignee: The declaration requires the inclusion of the consignee's code, name, and address to facilitate the identification of the party responsible for the goods upon arrival.
Vessel: The cargo declaration must specify the transport mode, vessel name, and nationality for tracking and clearance purposes.
Goods Description: Detailed information about the goods, such as package types, weights, volume, container counts, and descriptions, is required in the cargo declaration.
Value: The declaration must include precise valuation details including freight amounts, insurance, and the value for customs purposes, along with the relevant currency for each.

member_objects.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) সনদ এর মেয়াদ, নবায়ন ও পরিবর্তন

Authorized Economic Operator: The recognition certificate for an Authorized Economic Operator is valid for a period of one year.
An Authorized Economic Operator must apply for the renewal of their certificate within a specified period after its expiration by submitting updated documentation as required.
The relevant authority will verify the renewal application and conduct post-clearance onsite audits before renewing the certificate, with a reporting obligation to the committee.
Failure to apply for renewal in a timely manner may result in the temporary suspension of Authorized Economic Operator benefits, subject to specific conditions regarding audit delays.
An Authorized Economic Operator must maintain the standards and criteria upon which their recognition was granted.

Any significant business changes, such as legal status, name, address, operational nature, accounting systems, management, or physical premises, must be reported to the designated authority within a set timeframe.
If a legal entity change occurs, the new entity must apply for a new certificate, which may lead to the cancellation of the old certificate after formal review.

Self-disclosure of customs-related errors by an Authorized Economic Operator will not negatively impact their recognition status unless the error involves serious offenses like tax evasion or smuggling.
In the event of a discovered error, the operator is required to investigate the cause and implement preventative measures to ensure future compliance.
